messages:
kevin: Heads-up — big enterprise asked for a per-tenant 'sentinel' routing header that forces their traffic to dedicated pools even when autoscaler would spill to hosted. Need opinions on safety/precedence.
maria: 👍 Why do they need force-route? is this about data isolation or perf predictability?
kevin: Both. They want guaranteed capacity and lower tail-latency. Their SLAs demand us to never fall back to hosted even during short spikes.
jon: That worries me. If we allow a header to override smart routing we risk customers bypassing cost-aware policies. Also could starve others if abused.
sujay: We can gate it behind enterprise entitlements + quota reservation. Implementation idea: header X-Redwood-Sentinel: tenant:<id>;policy:pin
maria: Entitlements + quota reservation sounds fine. Also need audit trail and console toggle to disable per-org sentinel for ops.
jon: Agree on audit. Also need a precedence table: request-level pin -> org policy -> route config -> global fallback. And pinned routing must respect capacity hard limits.
kevin: What should the API gateway do if pinned pool is saturated? Reject or queue? Customer wants no hosted fallback.
sujay: Two options: 1) Reject with 429 + structured body explaining 'pinned pool saturated' so caller can retry. 2) Queue short-lived (but that affects latency). I'd lean 429 for clarity.
maria: 429 plus metrics/alerts. Also need a console UX: per-customer routing policy page that shows current pinned pools, reserved capacity, recent rejects. Product to own.
jon: Implementation detail: we should not rely on raw headers from public apps. Only accept sentinel if request signed with org token or coming from private network. Otherwise header spoofing risk.
kevin: +1. Validate header by verifying signature header X-Redwood-Sentinel-Sig using org key. Make gateway reject unsigned sentinel headers.
sujay: Here's a prototype config snippet for the gateway (for discussion):
```
route_overrides:
  - match: "org.id == 'acme-corp'"
    sentinel:
      enabled: true
      require_signature: true
      pinned_pool: "dedicated-acme-v2"
      on_full: "reject"
```
jon: Nice. We also need telemetry: per-org 'pinned_rejects', 'pinned_evicts', 'pinned_success_pct' exported to datadog and surfaced in console.
kevin: Ops question — who can flip sentinels in emergencies? Need a breakglass path with approval audit.
maria: Security/Legal requested that any per-org override change emits an audit log entry and an automated email to account owner + security. Also record in change history in console.
sujay: Dev plan: gate feature behind RBAC + entitlement checks, implement signature validation in gateway, add quota reservation extension in quota service, add metrics. Rollout: alpha for 2 enterprise customers, then gradual.
jon: One more: add a denylist too. If org is on denylist, ignore sentinel headers entirely and log. Useful for misuse cases.
kevin: Sounds good. Action items: @jon to spec precedence and signature validation by EOD Fri, @sujay to mock gateway config and metrics, @maria to draft console UX and security notif flow. :eyes:
infra-bot: deploy-gateway 2026-03-17T14:12:07Z: Canary rollout started for branch feature/sentinel-policy (canary=2/10 hosts)
kevin: Thanks — will sync with sales on the customer expectations and confirm SLA wording before we enable.
